statement: Wisp must compile code-backed project context without losing Monokl's resolution uncertainty, provenance, scope, or freshness and without allowing incremental or historical heuristics to become alternate truth.
stakeholder: A coding agent or reviewer consuming an implementation, review, or architecture briefing.
why: A briefing can be concise yet unsafe if it turns candidates into facts, mixes partial refresh generations, serves stale incremental state, or treats Git history as a dependency graph.
done_when: Every code-backed result preserves resolved, ambiguous, unresolved, or external status, candidate identities where present, resolver provenance, precision, scope, and content/workspace identity.
Readers observe only a complete derived-state publication and a failed refresh leaves the prior complete publication usable.
Generated incremental change sequences produce the same canonical derived state as a clean rebuild after every step.
Any Git-history ranking signal remains separately typed, explainable, non-authoritative, and disabled by default until a Prism ablation demonstrates benefit.
out_of_scope: Implementing parsers, language servers, or a second code index in Wisp
Treating co-change or ownership as proof of dependency
Changing the canonical workflow artifact formats
Mandating a generation table for writes that already publish in one transaction
